claim: Portrait fan compression had no legibility floor and degraded to an 8pt strip, making buried ranks unreadable.
note: Core handled (the 8pt/12pt sliver is gone; I verified the arithmetic: with w = floor(maxH/(aspect + 0.42*(n-1))), column()'s floor((maxH-cardH)/(n-1)) lands at ~0.42w for the tallest column, and the max(8,...) backstop only binds past ~27 cards, so it is genuinely dead). Landscape provably never triggers the shrink: 0.42/cardAspect = 0.42/1.6727 = 0.251 < landscapeFan 0.34, so cardW*units <= landscapeBoardH always. REMAINING EDGE: the 0.42 constant is derived from a wrong text-layout model. The comment at ContentView.swift:400-401 assumes the rank glyph starts at the 0.05*w top padding, but CardView renders the rank as a Text whose line box (~1.17em tall) sits at the padding top, and SF's ascent-to-cap gap (ascent 0.955em - cap 0.714em = 0.241em at a 0.50*w font = 0.12*w) pushes the cap DOWN. The digit therefore spans ~0.17w..0.53w, not 0.05w..0.41w -- which is exactly what round 0 measured independently (y=7..22 at cardW=41 => 0.17w..0.53w). A 0.42w floor hides the bottom ~30% of the rank cap. To actually show the whole digit the constant must be ~0.53 (0.05 + 0.955*0.50); note that raising it also lowers the column count at which the card-size shrink kicks in, which interacts with the new finding below.

claim: The web prototype's demo bar wires BOTH 'Stop' and the post-line 'Done' to stopDemo() (index.html:1563), which only clears the demoing flag and hides the bar -- it never re-deals. So the exact exploit the iOS side just spent two rounds closing is wide open on the web, and it needs no corrupt data: click 'Show me how to win', let the baked line auto-play 90% of the deal, click Stop, and the 95%-solved board is immediately playable again (startDrag's only gate is `isWon() || demoing`, index.html:512). The next manual move sets startTime=Date.now() from scratch (index.html:679, 722) and, on completion, onWin -> recordWin writes wins[seed] with secs measured from that moment -- a fabricated best time plus a solved-deal checkmark on a deal the player never solved. Auto-finish makes it one click (canOfferFinish only needs startTime, index.html:914). The iOS code comment at ContentView.swift:479-482 states this is forbidden behaviour; the web copy does it.
note: CONFIRMED by reading the code, not run. Pre-existing and web-side, so a scoped deferral to BACKLOG (like DV-1) is a defensible answer -- but the loop should record it, because the just-landed iOS fix makes the two copies diverge on an integrity rule that tests/ios-parity.test.mjs exists to keep in sync. Fix shape: point demoStop.onclick at restartDeal (matching ios ContentView.swift:483).

claim: The web applyDemoToken (index.html:1236-1247) still has every defect just removed from the Swift copy: `case 'C'` does cells[cells.indexOf(null)]=card, so with no free cell it writes cells[-1] and the popped card vanishes from the deck; `case 'F'/'C'` pop() an empty column, yielding undefined and throwing on card.suit. That throw happens inside the setTimeout demoTick, so it escapes silently, the timer chain dies with demoing stuck true, and startDrag early-returns forever -- input is permanently locked until reload. index.html:473 already documents this exact lockup as a known hazard. Web finishDemo (index.html:1280) also has no boardComplete guard, the counterpart of the guard just added at Game.swift:865.
note: Same reachability caveat as the original iOS finding (needs malformed baked data, and all 922 shipped lines are clean), so this is a parity/defence-in-depth item, not a live bug. Only worth doing together with the index.html:demo-stop finding above.

claim: The new card-size shrink applies to the tableau only, and the tableau HStack is content-sized inside a full-width GeometryReader in a VStack(alignment: .leading), so once it triggers the whole tableau becomes narrower and hugs the LEFT edge while the foundations/free cells above stay at the original width: on a 375pt phone with a 15-card column, w drops 41->33 and the tableau is 8*33+7*4=292pt against the upper row's 356pt, leaving a 64pt dead margin down the right side of the board. Worse, w is recomputed every body pass from game.tableau.map(\.count).max(), so every move that changes the tallest column's height re-scales ALL 52 tableau cards (~2.6pt per card at the threshold) inside the caller's withAnimation -- the whole board pulses and re-flows horizontally on single-card moves, which is precisely the 'no whole-board resize as one column grows' property the replaced comment at ContentView.swift:429-434 used to guarantee.
note: CONFIRMED by reading the layout, not run. Kept at minor because of reachability: I computed the trigger threshold as cardW*(1.6727 + 0.42*(n-1)) > maxH, which needs roughly a 14-20 card column (375x667 with the HUD bar up: maxH ~316 => n>=16; 393x852 with HUD: maxH ~418 => n>=20; 320x568: n>=14). Note the threshold DROPS if the 0.42 constant is corrected upward per the legibility finding, so fix the two together. Two cheap mitigations: centre the tableau (.frame(maxWidth: .infinity) on the HStack) so it stays aligned with the upper row, and quantise w (e.g. step in 4pt buckets or derive it from a monotonically-latched max column count) so a single move cannot re-scale the board. SUSPECTED extra: on a transient maxH == 0 layout pass the guard falls through to max(30, floor(0)) = 30, so all tableau cards would briefly render at the 30pt minimum -- previously such a pass only collapsed the fan, not the card size.

claim: The drift-guard re-pin quietly dropped coverage: the old F pin was 'let c = tableau[n(1)].removeLast()', which asserted that F reads its column from field 1. The new pin is 'let c = tableau[col].removeLast()' and nothing pins 'let col = n(1)', so an edit changing F (or C) to read n(2) as the column would keep all five pins green while making the iOS demo replay a baked line differently from index.html and tools/solver -- the precise divergence this file exists to catch.
note: The rest of the re-pin is legitimate -- the T pin is unchanged and the two-line C pin is as strong as the one it replaced. One-line fix: add 'let col = n(1)' to the snippet list. Verified npm test is 67/67 green as claimed.
